newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-South Australian grains dispute resolved.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-South Australian grains dispute resolved.

text.p: Work bans which delayed loading of grain onto three ships off South Australia were lifted on Friday after agreement was reached in an industrial dispute at South Australia Cooperative Bulk Handling (SACBH) terminals.

Australian Workers Union State secretary Bob Sneath told Reuters about 400 workers at Wallaroo, Port Pirie, Ardrossan, Port Giles, Port Lincoln and Thevenard terminals all had lifted bans and resumed normal work by early Friday afternoon.

The SACBH said the two-day dispute had interrupted loading of three wheat vessels - the Lubaansgracht bound for New Zealand with 5,000 tonnes, Orion Glory for Papua New Guinea with 16,000 tonnes and Pylos for Yemen with 16,000 tonnes.
Sneath said "a couple" of farmers had been prevented from unloading grain into silos.
There had been fears the dispute, which had simmered for the nine months, could severely disrupt the State's estimated 5.4 million tonnes 1996/97 harvest which began earlier this week.
SACBH general manager Michael Thomas said a two year agreement on wage rises and productivity improvements had been signed and accepted by workers.
